inspected_statements.statement: A central extension with a conjugacy-equivariant section of the specified inertia subset defines its lifting invariant by multiplying the selected lifts.
inspected_statements.application: The explicit commuting double transpositions in Proposition 2 have anticommuting spin lifts, so the required section does not exist for the ordinary spin cover.

inspected_statements.locator: Theorem 7.6.1 and preceding definition of sufficiently large
inspected_statements.statement: For a fixed finite group and fixed inertia subset, sufficiently large multiplicities give the stable component description; the stated largeness condition applies in each inertia class.
inspected_statements.application: This fixed-group theorem does not prove uniform transitivity for growing A_n; in the all-branch-class formulation the distinguished long-cycle multiplicity is one.

sources.role: Context and definition; no imported connectivity theorem is used in the finite n=10 proof.
sources.limits: The note proves only failure of the ordinary spin sign and the killing of its central kernel, not a classification of all reduced Schur multipliers. It does not infer higher-degree braid connectivity from the stabilization theorem.
